claims.claim_ar: يُقْرَأُ «الَّذِينَ» مَعَ وَاوِ العاطِفِ (أي يَجُوزُ قراءتها بِالوَاوِ باعتبارها معطوفة على صيغة سابقة).
claims.claim_en: The relative clause particle «الَّذِينَ» can be read with a prefixed waw (i.e. read as part of «وَالَّذِينَ...»), allowing it to be treated as conjoined/ma'tuf in some readings.
claims.needs_review_reason: The cited passage discusses the form «وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا» in another verse; applicability to the present ayah (which begins with «وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ…») is plausible but not explicitly stated in the source and should be reviewed.

claims.source_quote_ar: قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: (مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) : مُبْتَدَأٌ، وَالْخَبَرُ مَحْذُوفٌ
claims.claim_ar: في تركيبٍ مثل «مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا» يعتبر «مَثَلُ…» مبتدأً والخبر محذوفًا؛ يبيّن ذلك أن تراكيب «الَّذِينَ + جملةٍ» قد تدخل في جملٍ اسمية يُحذف خبرها.
claims.claim_en: In the construction «مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا», «مَثَلُ…» is treated as the subject (mubtada') and the predicate (khabar) is omitted; this shows that constructions with «الَّذِينَ + clause» can function within nominal sentences with an omitted predicate.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source example is from a different verse and concerns the specific pattern «مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ…»; extension of this rule to the present ayah (which has an explicit predicate) is an inference that requires verification.
